paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Paul is not putting a lock on the cookie jar. He says it himself: "I am saying this for your own good, not to restrict you, but in order to promote proper decorum and undivided devotion to the Lord." (1 Corinthians 7:35) Marriage is good, singleness is good, and Paul never calls either one a sin (1 Corinthians 7:28, 7:36).

So what's the point? Paul says "the time is short," and "this world in its present form is passing away." (1 Corinthians 7:29, 7:31) That's why he wants them free from concern, with their hearts pointed at the Lord and not tangled up in the things of this world. The unmarried are concerned about the work of the Lord, and the married have divided interests, because loving a spouse is real work, and it's good work (1 Corinthians 7:32-34).

Now here's what I want you to carry out of my bakery, baker. Whatever your situation is, married, single or widowed, ask how you can give the Lord your undivided devotion right where you are. Hold everything else loosely, even the good stuff, because the Lord is the one thing that doesn't pass away. And notice how Paul handles a question where he has no command from the Lord: he says so plainly, he gives his judgment as one the Lord's mercy has made trustworthy, and he tells them that marrying does well and not marrying does even better (1 Corinthians 7:25, 7:38).
